{{Short description|German virologist}}

'''Thomas Iftner''' (born 27 July 1958 in [[Fürth]]) is a German [[virologist]]. He heads the Institute for Medical Virology and Epidemiology of Viral Diseases at the [https://www.medizin.uni-tuebingen.de/en-de/startseite University Hospital] [[Tübingen]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Thomas Iftner {{!}} Universitätsklinikum Tübingen |url=https://www.medizin.uni-tuebingen.de/de/das-klinikum/mitarbeiter/profil/1617 |access-date=2023-11-20 |website=www.medizin.uni-tuebingen.de}}</ref>

His research interests in the field of [[Papillomaviridae|papillomaviruses]] range from basic research and animal models to clinical studies and molecular epidemiology, with over 200 publications.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Suerbaum |first1=Sebastian |title=Medizinische Mikrobiologie und Infektiologie |last2=Hahn |first2=Helmut |last3=Burchard |first3=Gerd-Dieter |last4=Kaufmann |first4=Stefan H. == Life and work ==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=January 2024}}
Thomas Iftner received his diploma in biology in 1985 and his doctorate from the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg|University of Erlangen]] in 1988. His postgraduate training included a research fellowship at the [[University of California, Los Angeles|University of California]], Dept. of Microbiology and Immunology, Los Angeles, USA. From 1990 to 1997 he was at the University of Erlangen, where he [[Habilitation|habilitated]] in 1993. From 1997 to 2018, he was a full professor at the [[University of Tübingen|Eberhard Karls University of Tübingen]] and head of the Research Section for Experimental Virology. In April 2018, he took over as head of the Institute of Medical Virology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Thomas Iftner |url=https://www.medizin.uni-tuebingen.de/de/das-klinikum/mitarbeiter/profil/1617}}</ref> He founded the [[Molecular medicine|Molecular Medicine]] programs in 2006 at the University of Tübingen and was dean of studies for Molecular Medicine from 2006 to 2017. From 2009 to 2020, he was also Vice Dean in the Faculty of Medicine. Furthermore, he has been an associate professor at [[James Cook University]], Townsville, Australia, since 2009.

After activities as co-founder and director of the European Consortium Against Cervical Cancer (ECCA, Lyon, France), Iftner has been chairman and initiator of the Zervita project group since 2006,<ref>{{cite web |title=ZERVITA - HPV - Gebärmutterhalskrebs: ZERVITA informiert |url=https://www.zervita.de/zervita/index.php |website=zervita.de |access-date=7 March 2024 |language=de}}</ref> whose aim is to inform the public in Germany about risk factors, prevention, early detection and treatment of cervical carcinoma and its precursors, as well as about human papillomaviruses. He belonged to expert groups of the [[International Agency for Research on Cancer]] (IARC) in Lyon, for the preparation of the monograph on cervical cancer prevention and papillomaviruses, in which the valid risk classification of HPV genotypes was established, and the "Cervical Cancer Screening Handbook" and was a member of the board of directors "International Papillomavirus Society" (IPVS).

The multinational cohort study<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dillner |first=J. |last2=Rebolj |first2=M. |last3=Birembaut |first3=P. |last4=Petry |first4=K.-U. |last5=Szarewski |first5=A. |last6=Munk |first6=C. |last7=de Sanjose |first7=S. |last8=Naucler |first8=P. |last9=Lloveras |first9=B. |last10=Kjaer |first10=S. |last11=Cuzick |first11=J. |last12=van Ballegooijen |first12=M. |last13=Clavel |first13=C. |last14=Iftner |first14=T. |date=2008-10-13 |title=Long term predictive values of cytology and human papillomavirus testing in cervical cancer screening: joint European cohort study |url=https://www.bmj.com/lookup/doi/10.1136/bmj.a1754 |journal=BMJ |language=en |volume=337 |issue=oct13 1 |pages=a1754–a1754 |doi=10.1136/bmj.a1754 |issn=0959-8138|pmc=2658827 }}</ref> by Iftner and Dillner was one of the seminal papers for the American guidelines on cervical cancer screening. He is a member of the [[American Society for Microbiology|American Society of Microbiology]], the German Society of Virology and member of the COMSTECH distinguished scholar program of the OIC.
